In that situation, the subdivision (a) exemption is not additionally available.

results.derivation_summary: Under Craddock, a Texas default judgment should be set aside and a new trial granted when the defendant shows three things: (1) the failure to answer before judgment was not intentional or the result of conscious indifference, but was due to mistake or accident; (2) the motion for new trial sets up a meritorious defense; and (3) the motion is filed at a time when granting it will cause no delay or other injury to the plaintiff. Procedurally, the motion must be filed before or within thirty days after the judgment is signed (Rule 329b(a)), and if the court does not sign a written order deciding it within seventy-five days of the judgment, it is overruled by operation of law (Rule 329b(c)). Because each element turns on the particular facts the movant presents, the outcome is a case-by-case judicial determination rather than an automatic result.

results.derivation_summary: Under Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 16.004(a), a suit on a debt must be filed no later than four years after the cause of action accrues. Debt is expressly listed in subsection (a)(3) among the actions governed by this four-year period. So a collection lawsuit on a consumer debt in Texas must be brought within four years of accrual of the claim. The text does not specify when accrual occurs for a particular debt, so that determination would depend on other authority.
